chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from al-Halabi, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: that he was asked about a muhsan man who committed illicit intercourse with a woman, and three men and two women testified against him. He said:

He said: ‘If three men and two women testify against him, stoning becomes obligatory upon him. But if two men and four women testify against him, their testimony is not admissible and he is not stoned; rather, he is given the hadd of the fornicator.’

key_terms.رِجَالٍ: male witnesses in the evidentiary requirement
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُمْ: their legal testimony or witness statement
key_terms.شَهِدَ: gave testimony or bore witness in a legal case
key_terms.ٱلرَّجْمُ: stoning as the legal punishment for a muhsan adulterer
key_terms.ٱمْرَأَتَانِ: two female witnesses counted alongside male witnesses

ai.seo_question: What number and composition of witnesses establish rajm in a zina case according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the evidentiary threshold in establishing zina for a muhsan offender. It distinguishes between forms of testimony that establish rajm and those that do not, while still allowing a lesser hadd punishment in the latter case.
